Same root cause on Windows Desktop **1.18.23** → Linux `opencode serve` (server at `<internal-host>`, project at `<internal-path>/work-projects`).

The remote connection itself works: server returns 401 without creds (basic auth), and the client receives server events (turn-complete notifications land in `opencode.global.dat` for the configured server URL). But the Home UI never lists the remote project/sessions.

Decisive log line from the bundled sidecar (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`):

```
bootstrapping directory="C:\home\srv\projects\work-projects"
ERROR PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (/home/srv/projects/work-projects)
  cause: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat 'C:\home'
```

So the Windows client translates the server-native POSIX path `/home/srv/projects/work-projects` into `C:\home\srv\projects\work-projects` and tries to `realPath` it locally → ENOENT → project/session list never loads.

Notes:
- Same server + same credentials work fine from macOS Desktop client — macOS doesn't do the drive-letter translation.
- The desktop even created `opencode.workspace.-home-srv-pr.*.dat` workspace state for the remote project path, confirming it treats the remote worktree as a local workspace.
- Duplicate family: #29766, #36064, #42627, #44216.

I hit this in production and built a deterministic reproduction plus a tested fix. Sharing the evidence since this issue currently has no repro.

## Deterministic reproduction

A minimal OpenAI-compatible SSE server that opens the assistant role and then closes on `stop` without ever sending a content delta:

```
data: {"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant"},"finish_reason":null}]}
data: {"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}
data: [DONE]
```

Point a provider at it and run any prompt. Reproduces 3/3 on `1.18.23` (Homebrew binary) and from source on `dev` @ `902e67e`, so it is not a packaging artifact:

```json
{"type":"step_start","part":{"type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"step_finish","part":{"type":"step-finish","reason":"stop",
  "tokens":{"input":0,"output":0,"reasoning":0,"cache":{"write":0,"read":0}},"cost":0}}
```

Exit code 0, no error event, no WARN/ERROR log line. The assistant message is persisted with `finish: "stop"` and only `step-start` / `step-finish` parts.

## Production occurrences

From my local session database, assistant turns with `finish: "stop"` and no text, tool, or reasoning part:

| Provider / model | Turns |
|---|---|
| gpt-5.6-terra | 7 |
| claude-sonnet-5 | 2 |
| gpt-5.6-luna | 1 |
| claude-opus-4-8 | 1 |

Four models across two families, all through one OpenAI-compatible gateway. Query used:

```sql
SELECT json_extract(m.data,'$.modelID') AS model, COUNT(*)
FROM message m
WHERE json_extract(m.data,'$.role') = 'assistant'
  AND json_extract(m.data,'$.finish') = 'stop'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM part p WHERE p.message_id = m.id
                  AND json_extract(p.data,'$.type') IN ('text','tool','reasoning'))
GROUP BY model;
```

All of them report `input=0, output=0`, so nothing was accounted for — the request produced no usage at all.

## Why #41466 does not cover this

PR #41466 (rebase of #40531) guards only unknown finish reasons:

```ts
if (ctx.assistantMessage.finish === "unknown" && !generated) { ... }
```

Every occurrence above finishes with `stop`, so that guard never fires for them. Confirmed by cherry-picking #41466 onto `dev` and rerunning the repro: still silent.

## A second, opposite defect from the same place

While reproducing, the `unknown` variant turned out to fail the other way. Same server, only `finish_reason` changed to a non-standard value that normalizes to `unknown`:

| Repro mode | Requests to the fake provider |
|---|---|
| `finish_reason: "stop"` | 2, then silent success |
| non-standard reason → `unknown` | **2517 before I killed it** |

It never terminates. Both behaviors trace to `prompt.ts`:

```ts
const finished = handle.message.finish && !["tool-calls", "unknown"].includes(handle.message.finish)
```

`stop` counts as finished, so the loop breaks without ever checking whether the turn produced output. `unknown` never counts as finished, so the loop keeps re-requesting. Neither branch asks the question that matters: *did this turn generate anything?*

Note this is the turn loop, not `SessionRetry.policy` — the policy already bounds at `RETRY_MAX_RETRIES`. The two retry levels are distinct.

I could not find an existing issue for the unbounded `unknown` case (#15533 is auto-compaction, #17648 predates the current bound). Happy to file it separately if that is preferred.

## Tested fix

Guarding on *output produced* rather than on the finish reason covers both. In `processor.ts`, track whether the stream opened any content block and fail the attempt when it did not:

```ts
const EMPTY_TURN_FINISH = new Set(["stop", "unknown"])

// in the stream tap
if (event.type === "text-start" || event.type === "reasoning-start" ||
    event.type === "tool-input-start" || event.type === "tool-call") generated = true

// after runDrain
if (!generated && !ctx.needsCompaction && EMPTY_TURN_FINISH.has(ctx.assistantMessage.finish ?? "")) {
  yield* new SessionRetry.EmptyResponseError({ ... })
}
```

Then make `EmptyResponseError` retryable by iden
Filed the unbounded `unknown` case separately as #45315, since it is a distinct failure mode (never terminates) even though it shares the predicate described above.

Thanks for the references — read through both.

**#38470**: its root cause (confirmed in the thread, with [PR #41728](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/41728)) is that `opencode serve` runs with `instance: false`, so the lazy `Plugin`/`InstanceState` bootstrap that initializes MCP never runs for a bare `POST /api/session` HTTP session — unlike the TUI or `opencode run`, which both trigger that bootstrap. That's a different mechanism from what I found here: in my reproduction, `GET /mcp` already reports the server as `connected` (MCP is live and populated) for the exact session that still gets no MCP tools. So this isn't an initialization-timing gap — `ToolRegistry.materialize()` in `packages/core/src/tool/registry.ts` (the V2 registry backing `/api/session/{id}/prompt`) structurally only sources built-in `ApplicationTools` and local registrations; there's no MCP merge step in that file at all, regardless of whether MCP itself is already up. PR #41728 also only touches `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/serve.ts`, so it wouldn't affect this V2 path either way.

**#33027**: same user-visible symptom (connected but not exposed), but no source-level cause was pinned down there (older version, TUI, and the issue itself notes the binary couldn't be inspected directly) — I can't tell from it whether it's the same gap or something else.

So: #38470 looks related but distinct (different code path, already has a proposed fix that doesn't touch V2's `ToolRegistry`), and #33027 is inconclusive relative to this one. Happy to have maintainers merge/link these as they see fit — just wanted to share what the V2 trace actually shows in case it's useful for triage.

This is not correct.

Thanks for the report. There appears to be a misunderstanding about the discovery API: Code Mode's instructions specify **`search(...)`**, not **`tools.search(...)`**.

For reference, in the V2 source:

- The [catalog instructions](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/ded8a492d142d599e59c9d1bf18d3eff688df01f/packages/core/src/codemode/instructions.ts#L9-L17) tell the model to use `search` when the catalog is partial. The [signature inserted into those instructions](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/ded8a492d142d599e59c9d1bf18d3eff688df01f/packages/codemode/src/tool-runtime.ts#L426-L430) explicitly starts with `search(input: ...)`, without a `tools.` prefix.
- The [interpreter registers `search` as a separate global](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/ded8a492d142d599e59c9d1bf18d3eff688df01f/packages/codemode/src/interpreter/runtime.ts#L300-L306), alongside `tools`; it is not a tool under `tools`.
- An [existing test](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/ded8a492d142d599e59c9d1bf18d3eff688df01f/packages/codemode/test/codemode.test.ts#L732-L762) exercises `search(...)` against a Context7-shaped tool and checks the returned signature.

The discovery call inside `execute` should therefore be:

```js
return await search({
  namespace: "context7",
  query: "resolve library",
  limit: 10,
})
```

An `Unknown tool 'search'.` error from `tools.search(...)` does not demonstrate that the documented discovery function is missing; it calls a different path.

We're closing this as **cannot reproduce as reported**. If you can share an actual session transcript showing OpenCode instructing the model to call `tools.search(...)`, or the correct `search(...)` call failing, we'll investigate further. Please include the exact instructions, tool-call input, and returned output, with credentials and private information redacted.
